text:
maria: Heads up — found a replay bug when we normalize path before deduping query params. If /v1/foo/ and /v1/foo get rewritten, we can end up with duplicate client_id when we also inject headers.
dan: Can you paste the minimal rule so I can reproduce?
maria: Sure:
```yaml
- match: ^/v1/(.*)
  normalize_trailing_slash: remove
  query_dedupe: keep-first
  inject_headers:
    - name: x-client-id
      from: query.client_id
```
dan: keep-first breaks when upstream passes client_id in both header and query — should prefer header override, otherwise downstream sees two sources.
sara: My vote: ordering should be explicit and documented: path normalization -> sensitive query strip -> query dedupe -> header injection -> final header scrub. That keeps injected headers deterministic.
elaine: Telemetry note: emit a rewrite tag when we change query behavior (rewrite.query_behavior) and include original vs final query count. Helps detect regressions in production.
maria: Also we need a console toggle for canarying rewrite behaviors per-route: e.g., query_dedupe=keep-first|keep-last|allow-multi. Engineers want to flip without a deploy.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: rewrite-service v3.14 -> canary 10% @ 1764520500 :rocket:
sara: I'll open a tiny PR that implements the ordering & telemetry fields + a feature flag hook. gh: https://github.com/redwood/rewrite-service/pull/482
maria: Please add unit tests for double-encoded params and a case where upstream proxies append a client_id header.
dan: Also add a test ensuring pre-signed-url params (sig, expires) are preserved if a route opts into passthrough-signature.
elaine: For rollout UX: console should show count of routes using each behavior and a histogram of client-side error spikes after toggle. That will make PMs less nervous.
sara: Agreed. I'll land the PR behind a feature flag and wire the console toggle to the rollout API.
maria: Nice. After canary we should run the redirect+query dedupe analyzer job on traffic sample to validate no regressions.
dan: +1. I'll take the analyzer job.
maria: Thanks everyone.
